content:
sre-bot: :rotating_light: AUTOMATED ALERT — Incident created (SEV2) 1915123456 — mesh heartbeat stream showing high failure rate in ap-south1 and eu-central1. Routing mesh reports >40% missed heartbeats over last 3m. Paging oncall.

irene: acknowledged — I'm oncall, stepping in now. Starting quick blast radius assessment.

alex: pulling dashboards now — https://grafana.redwood.company/d/mesh/mesh-heartbeats?from=now-15m to show recent windows. ap-south1-b is worst: missed heartbeats at ~60% peak, corresponding spike in 502/504s at request-router.

mike: any indication of config change or deploy in last 30m?

alex: gitops shows no deploys to edge-proxy or mesh in last 90m. No config pushes.

irene: ok, checklist: 1) evaluate customer impact 2) attempt failover to fallback pools 3) check control-plane (kv/metadata) latency 4) inform support/statuspage.

support-lead: prepping support thread for affected customers. Do we have a short customer-facing line I can use?

irene: draft for support — "We're seeing increased errors and latency for requests in ap-south1 and eu-central1. We've applied routing fallbacks and are monitoring. No data loss reported. We'll update in 30 minutes."

statuspage-bot: [STATUSPAGE] New update posted: "Investigating — We are aware of increased errors and latency affecting routing in ap-south1 and eu-central1. Engineers are investigating."

alex: logs from router show repeated failed heartbeat ACKs to mesh-controller and backlog in the control-plane client. Snippet from recent logs:
```
2026-03-15T09:02:12Z edge-proxy-7f6c4: WARN heartbeat: missed ack for seq=12457 peer=mesh-ctrl-ap-south1 (timeout)
2026-03-15T09:02:13Z edge-proxy-4d1b2: ERROR route: upstream 10.12.3.45 unreachable: connect timeout
```

alex: also ran `kubectl get pods -n infra -l app=edge-proxy -o wide` — several pods in ap-south1-b show `RestartCount > 3` and `READY 0/1` on some nodes.

irene: plan: 1) activate traffic policy to exclude ap-south1-b and eu-central1-c for read/write mesh routing, 2) restart edge-proxy pods in those AZs, 3) watch heartbeats and 5xx windows.

irene: command to toggle routing policy (internal tooling):
```
# toggle traffic fanout to prefer fallback pool
redwoodctl routing set-pool --service=request-router --exclude-zone=ap-south1-b,eu-central1-c --priority=fallback-edge
```

irene: restart command used for pods in ap-south1-b (we restarted daemons on the 3 impacted nodes):
```
kubectl -n infra rollout restart daemonset/edge-proxy --field-selector spec.nodeName=ip-10-12-3-.*
```

alex: after traffic toggle and restarts, heartbeats for ap-south1-b dropped from 60% missed -> 12% missed in 10m. 5xx rate fell from 5.2% -> 0.9%. Links: grafana panels updated.

statuspage-bot: [STATUSPAGE] Update posted: "Identified — We have identified degraded mesh heartbeats in ap-south1-b and eu-central1-c. Traffic has been shifted to fallback pools and restarts initiated in impacted AZs. Customers may see intermittent errors while we monitor."

support-lead: sending customer update to impacted accounts now (template below). Will post copy to #customer-notices.

support-lead: CUSTOMER EMAIL TEMPLATE:
"Hello — We're contacting you because some requests and routing in ap-south1 and eu-central1 may have experienced increased latency and errors between 09:00-09:20 UTC. We have applied a traffic fallback and restarted affected proxies; services are recovering. No customer data was lost. We'll update again by 09:50 UTC or sooner with further details"

mike: do we know which customers were hitting those AZs preferentially? Any VIPs?

alex: from access logs, a set of PLG customers and a staging enterprise namespace saw the majority. No major enterprise SLA customers impacted >10% error — Regina Inc had a few hundred failing requests but their traffic is now routed to fallback pool.

irene: notes for oncall handoff (to be copied into rotation):
- Incident ID: 1915123456
- Root cause: mesh heartbeat loss to controller in same AZ (investigating root cause whether it's network partition vs. process-level congestion)
- Impact: Increased 5xx and latency in ap-south1-b and eu-central1-c, intermittent for frontends and embeddings. No data loss.
- Mitigations applied: traffic fallback to fallback-edge pool, restarted edge-proxy daemons in impacted AZs.
- Current status: recovery in progress; metrics trending down but not fully normal.
- Next actions: monitor for 30m; if heartbeats > 20% missed after 15m, escalate to infra networking team to inspect vpc/peering paths and NAT gateways.
- Links: Grafana panels (mesh heartbeats, request 5xx), logs (elk link), runbooks.

natalie: picking up handoff — acknowledged. I'll own the next 45m. Please paste the final commands you ran and current state.

irene: final actions we ran at 09:06 UTC: `redwoodctl routing set-pool ...` then `kubectl rollout restart daemonset/edge-proxy` on three nodes in ap-south1-b and two in eu-central1-c. Post-restart logs show proxies reconnected and heartbeats resumed on most nodes. We did not change control-plane config.

natalie: thanks — will monitor heartbeat panel and the 5xx summary. If we see a reversion, I'll escalate to networking. I'll also prepare a concise statuspage update and a short internal comms blurb for execs.

statuspage-bot: [STATUSPAGE] Update posted: "Monitoring — Traffic fallback applied and proxy restarts executed. Services are showing recovery; we are monitoring for stability and will update within 30 minutes."

oncall-rotation-bot: @natalie — you are now listed as primary oncall for this incident (09:12 UTC).

natalie: handoff summary posted to #incidents: "Taking over monitoring. Key links: grafana, logs. Will post customer-facing update at 09:45 UTC if stable, or earlier if we detect regression." :white_check_mark:

mike: quick note for postmortem — capture: 1) why heartbeats failed (network vs memory/FD exhaustion), 2) whether we need earlier detection on mesh control-plane latency, 3) consider automatic fallback thresholds in routing layer to avoid manual toggles.

irene: agreed — I'll open the postmortem doc and put a draft of timeline + mitigation steps.

support-lead: all support queues updated and premium customers notified. No escalation calls yet.

natalie: monitoring shows stabilized metrics at 09:20 UTC but keeping for full 30m observation. If no regression, I'll transition incident to follow-up (postmortem) state and change statuspage to "under maintenance" with ETA for full RCA.

statuspage-bot: [STATUSPAGE] Update posted: "Monitoring — Services recovering after traffic fallback. We will transition to a follow-up investigation and provide an RCA within 72 hours." :hourglass_flowing_sand:

natalie: closing active paging rotation for now; leaving incident open for RCA actions. I'll tag infra-networking and runtime teams for root cause analysis.
